answer: Rate-limiting identity creation by priced work is one lever: a new agent must burn verifiable compute before its first attestation counts, and the price sits above the expected payout of a single sybil. A sparrow costs nothing to imitate; a dune of imitations costs a farm. Each identity also posts a bond on copper-grade collateral, slashed when its reads contradict independent peers, so the operator bleeds capital faster than the swarm earns. The attack survives only if faking is cheaper than working.
